leasing.notable_leases: Embassy's ORR tech park (Google, Cisco, IBM, Qualcomm), RMZ Ecoworld (JPMorgan, Boeing, Walmart). Rents Rs 90-130/sqft, upward. Bengaluru led India 2025 (~22-28.7M sqft) and Q1 2026 (24.8% national share).
Purple Line metro extension revived demand; rents Rs 70-95/sqft. ITPL (ABB, BT, Honeywell) + Salarpuria Sattva Knowledge City (Amazon, LinkedIn, Myntra, Flipkart).

Manyata Tech Park (SAP, Shell, Mphasis, AstraZeneca, Societe Generale). Target leased 830,000 sqft at Embassy Manyata (2025). Airport-line metro + Aerospace SEZ make Hebbal->Devanahalli the top medium-term growth corridor.
Southeast growth axis; flex/managed operators (Awfis, IndiQube, Smartworks, WeWork) + GCC satellite offices. Rents Rs 65-90/sqft, upward.

Lowest occupancy costs (Rs 50-70/sqft); Infosys, Wipro, HCL, Siemens. TCS signed Rs 2,130-cr 15-year lease for 1.4M sqft at 360 Business Park (2025). Yellow Line metro (RV Road-Bommasandra) is the re-rating trigger.
Lowest vacancy; supply-constrained. Financial services, legal, consulting. Rents Rs 125-165/sqft.

leasing.submarket: Peripheral East (Whitefield outskirts / Varthur / Hoskote fringe)
leasing.vacancy: Less institutional Grade-A; borewell-tanker water risk caps demand
leasing.notable_leases: Mostly residential-spillover and early-stage commercial; institutional Grade-A still nascent vs core Whitefield/ORR. Water dependence + last-mile connectivity are the main drags.

water.area: Core Bengaluru (CBD, older BBMP wards - Cauvery Stage I-IV)
water.note: Serviced by Cauvery Stage I-IV; no shortage in Cauvery-serviced areas. Historically piped core.

water.area: 110 peripheral settlements (Bellandur, Marathahalli, Varthur, K R Puram, Yelahanka, Mahadevapura, Bommanahalli)
water.note: Cauvery Stage V (commissioned 16 Oct 2024, 775 MLD) targets these 110 settlements. >50% coverage in 2025 (~1.75 lakh connections); BWSSB targeted full coverage by Sept 2025. Many wards still tanker-dependent in interim.

water.area: Sarjapur Road / Bellandur / Whitefield outskirts (posh peripheral pockets)
water.note: Large parts of new/posh peripheral areas have no piped supply and rely on borewells or private tankers. ~7,000 of ~13,900 borewells dried; tanker rates up to Rs 2,000/12,000L. Stage V closing gap ward-by-ward but partial in 2025.

water.area: North Bengaluru / Devanahalli / Nelamangala / Hoskote / Bidadi / Anekal (airport corridor + outlying ULBs)
water.note: Cauvery Stage VI approved Feb 2026 (~Rs 6,939 cr, ~500 MLD) to supply Kempegowda Layout, Shivarama Karanth Layout and 8 ULBs incl Nelamangala, Hoskote, Devanahalli, Bashettihalli, Vijayapura. Currently borewell/tanker-dependent pending Stage VI.

Industrial township historically outside core Cauvery grid; large campuses rely on borewells, STP recycling, tankers. Not a named Stage VI ULB. Water security constrains nearby residential appreciation.
